page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, providing two threads per core. The instance is equipped with 124.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4d-standard-32 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations. Multi-core performance is also highly competitive, with Geekbench multi-core scores in the top 10% and Passmark CPU scores in the top 25%. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16, alongside cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI, which contributes to strong performance in image processing, text processing, and software compilation.

Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both cached and uncached read/write operations fall within the average range, as do Redis SET operations and database transaction tests. However, the instance excels at lightweight LLM inference, achieving top-tier text generation speeds with smaller 135M parameter models. Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio, dedicated CPU allocation, and lack of local storage, this instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, web serving, software development pipelines, and CPU-bound analytical tasks.
